A SECOND SWEEP BESIDE `injection-sweep.json` BECAUSE IT RUNS A DIFFERENT
SUITE. That one breaks the READING rules and watches `ci-plan`'s own tests;
this one breaks THIS REPOSITORY — a flag in a workflow, a flag in a hook,
the ownership answer the workspace lister gives — and watches the gate that
walks the tree. Neither could be folded into the other: a manifest names one
test command, and a sweep that ran both suites for every injection would
spend the expensive one proving things the cheap one already proves.
THE FIRST FOUR ARE THE DEFECT ITSELF. On the tree this law arrived in, THIRTY
cargo commands resolved without `--locked`, so each of these puts one of them
back and asks whether anybody notices.
THE SUITE IS ADDRESSED AS A MODULE OF `all` AND NOT AS A TARGET. R1171 folded
seventy-six of the cli crate's test files into one binary, this file among
them; a `--test locked_resolution_smoke` after that commit is a name cargo
refuses outright, which takes the WHOLE sweep with it. The trailing filter
reproduces exactly the population this command had before the fold.

injections.name: a-workflow-step-resolves-freely
injections.why: this is the shape the gate was written for: a step that resolves without the flag rewrites a disagreeing lockfile before any later step in the same job can be asked about one

injections.name: a-git-hook-resolves-freely
injections.why: the hooks are the half of this repository's checks that no gate's population reached until R1115, and a developer meets them before CI does

injections.name: the-lister-stops-pinning-anything
injections.why: the workspace lister assembles its commands at runtime, so a flag can leave every one of them at once and no reading of its text would show it — this is why the gate reads what the lister PRINTS

injections.name: a-script-resolves-freely
injections.why: `scripts/gc` builds the whole workspace to warm the artifacts it is about to sweep; a free resolve there rewrites the root lockfile in the working tree of whoever ran it

injections.name: every-workspace-is-this-repositorys-to-pin
injections.why: `studio` resolves against the sibling `pinion` checkout. An ownership answer that never says so puts `--locked` on a workspace another repository's commit can break, and leaves the lockfile it cannot pin looking like one it should keep

injections.name: the-measured-fixture-agrees-with-its-manifest
injections.why: every claim about what cargo does to a lockfile rests on that fixture actually HOLDING a disagreement; if the version matches, a free resolve leaves the file alone and the measurement records `leaves it alone` for every subcommand there is

injections.name: the-tracked-shell-is-not-in-the-population
injections.why: three sources are bolted together here and dropping one takes the count down without taking it to zero — fifty compliant workflow commands read exactly like a clean repository, which is why the non-vacuity floor is per source rather than a total
